- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward surprise.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak or rises after trough), model often fails to adjust; align forecast with 3–5 day moving average of history.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently misreads sentiment trend; if sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.  
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.5–0.8), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast with 7-day weighted average.
